title: Why you should stop using a squat pad
summary: Short argument against using a squat pad. The pad is bulky and can roll up the back toward the neck when you lean forward, and it makes the bar unstable and staying tight harder. The upper back discomfort without it fades within weeks. Pads are fine for hip thrusts.

claims.claim: Stop using a pad when you squat.
Beginners use a squat pad because the bar hurts their upper back, but the pad is far more dangerous than that pain.
When lifters bend forward too much the bar wants to roll up the back toward the neck; a bulky pad that doesn't stay in place makes this worse and can pull you to the ground.
A pad makes the squat harder because it makes the bar unstable, and a stable, tight position is the most important thing to master in the squat; even velcro pads shift on your back.
The bar should sit tight against the skin of the upper back; that's also why squatting in many layers of clothing feels bad.
Squatting without a pad hurts the upper back for a couple of weeks to two months, then you stop feeling it and squatting feels ten times better.
Pads are indispensable for hip thrusts, unlike squats.
